scope: Three real PeerJS connections in isolated Chrome profiles on one machine/network. Not cross-network NAT, public hosting, or physical controller certification.
fixtures: QA hooks choose the host rare plan and its recipient deterministically; ordinary host simulation, PeerJS transport, guest input and snapshot handling run live. Bots are disabled and human spawn protection extended to isolate protocol behavior. The recipient disconnects through the normal leave path.

checks.name: Three isolated profiles establish real PeerJS connections
Simple policy arrives in both guest round setups
Simple host rejects a rare event
Insane policy arrives in both guest round setups
Guest cannot activate a rare event through the authority helper
Host ignores forged client rare-event and snapshot messages
Host-selected recipient and 30-round AK47 hydrate on both guests
Host and both guests switch to and play the rare WAV cue
Real guest keyboard input consumes authoritative AK47 ammo and propagates to witness
Recipient renders rare HUD and held AK47 without exception
Witness renders rare HUD and held AK47 without exception
Host removes departed recipient weapon and restores arena music
Surviving guest receives bot takeover, no AK47, and restored arena cue
Departing recipient returns to menu music
Host and guest ordinary weapon pools exclude AK47
No browser runtime exceptions during network scenario
Production source and audio hashes remain unchanged during the run
